specification.problem: Create an efficient transport channel from a fixed source site A to a fixed target site B in a disordered 2D discrete-time quantum walk by cutting links along a single line connecting A to B. The channel is carried by topologically protected chiral edge states, despite a vanishing bulk Chern number. The walk is realized as a periodically driven lattice Hamiltonian, and the relevant bulk invariant is the quasienergy winding.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the walk dynamics and the topological invariant, with a small finite lattice instance as an illustrative assumption. The paper's specific coin, shift and disorder model, cut geometry and numerical results are not reconstructed.

symbols.domain: unitary on lattice-site (position) tensor coin Hilbert space

symbols.meaning: Effective Floquet Hamiltonian for the periodically driven lattice
Quasienergy winding number, the bulk topological invariant

equations.label: Floquet operator
equations.description: The one-step walk operator is a unitary generated by the periodically driven Hamiltonian over period T. The quasienergy is defined by this relation.
equations.justification: Standard Floquet relation. The abstract states the walk is realized as a periodically driven lattice Hamiltonian, but not this form.
assumptions: Period T; H_F is the effective Hamiltonian from the log of U

equations.label: Vanishing Chern number
equations.description: The bulk Chern number of the system vanishes, so it cannot explain the edge states.
equations.abstract_quote: even though the bulk Chern number in this system vanishes

equations.label: Quasienergy winding invariant
equations.latex: W\neq 0\ \Rightarrow\ \text{chiral edge states along the cut}
equations.description: A nonzero quasienergy winding is the bulk invariant responsible for the chiral edge states that carry transport along the cut line.
equations.abstract_quote: identify the bulk topological invariant responsible for the edge states as the quasienergy winding of this Hamiltonian
equations.justification: The abstract names the winding as the responsible invariant. The explicit winding formula is not given.
assumptions: The precise winding integral formula is not specified

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Internal coin state determining shift direction

specification.initial_state: Walker localized at source site A with an assumed fixed coin state: |A>_pos |c0>_coin.

steps.description: Prepare the walker at site A with the initial coin state.
Apply the coin operation at each site (assumed, possibly with static disorder in coin angles).
Apply the conditional shift along lattice links, omitting shifts across links cut along the line from A to B (assumed reflection or no hopping at cuts).
Repeat the one-step operator U for t steps; transport along the cut is expected to follow chiral edge states.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after t steps, measure the walker position in the computational basis of the pos register (coin traced out), and estimate the arrival probability P_B(t)=sum_c |<B,c|U^t|A,c0>|^2 at target site B over repeated runs and disorder realizations.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average the estimated P_B(t) over disorder realizations and repeated shots. Compare cut-line against uncut configurations to assess channel efficiency, e.g. via maximum or time-resolved P_B(t). The abstract does not specify the observable.
assumptions: Bulk invariant formula and walk definition are not in the abstract.
Lattice size, coin dimension and register layout are illustrative assumptions.
Registers assumed as a 2D position lattice plus a 4-dimensional coin.
Measurement of arrival probability at B is an assumed observable, not stated in the abstract.
Arrival probability at B is used as the transport observable.
